title: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
text: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab is a PD-1 inhibitor. In KEYNOTE-024, 305 patients with untreated advanced NSCLC and PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50% or greater were randomized to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks (n=154) or platinum-based chemotherapy (n=151). RESULTS: Median progression-free survival was 10.3 months in the pembrolizumab group versus 6.0 months in the chemotherapy group (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.37-0.68; p<0.001). The overall survival rate at 6 months was 80.2% versus 72.4% (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.41-0.89; p=0.005). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 26.6% versus 53.3%. Immune-related adverse events included pneumonitis, colitis, and hepatitis. CONCLUSIONS: Pembrolizumab was associated with longer PFS and OS than platinum-based chemotherapy in this PD-L1 high NSCLC population (NCT02142738).

title: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
text: METHODS: Eligible patients had previously untreated stage IV NSCLC, no EGFR sensitizing mutation or ALK translocation, and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50% or greater. Pembrolizumab 200 mg was administered intravenously every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed according to RECIST 1.1. Overall survival was a key secondary endpoint. Sample size of 305 provided power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.55.

title: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
text: RESULTS: Among 305 randomized patients, median PFS was 10.3 months versus 6.0 months (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.37 to 0.68; p<0.001). Estimated overall survival at 6 months was 80.2% versus 72.4% (HR 0.60; p=0.005). Immune-related adverse events of any grade occurred more often with pembrolizumab, including pneumonitis 5.8%, colitis, and endocrinopathies. Grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events were less frequent with pembrolizumab (26.6%) than chemotherapy (53.3%).

title: Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma
text: BACKGROUND: CheckMate 067 compared nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab monotherapy, and ipilimumab monotherapy in untreated unresectable stage III or IV melanoma (n=945). Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg or nivolumab 3 mg/kg was given. RESULTS: Median PFS was 11.5 months with the combination versus 6.9 months with nivolumab and 2.9 months with ipilimumab (combination vs ipilimumab HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.31-0.57; p<0.001). Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 55.0% of combination patients, 16.3% of nivolumab, and 27.3% of ipilimumab, including diarrhea, colitis, transaminitis, and endocrine irAEs. CONCLUSIONS: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab and nivolumab alone had longer PFS than ipilimumab in untreated melanoma (NCT01844505).

title: Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma
text: In CheckMate 067, combination PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade improved PFS compared with CTLA-4 blockade alone (HR 0.42; p<0.001). PD-L1 expression was exploratory. Serious immune-related adverse events included colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, and hypophysitis. Median OS was not reached in the combination arm at the primary analysis. Mechanism: PD-1 blockade restores exhausted T-cell activity while CTLA-4 blockade enhances priming.

title: Atezolizumab for First-Line Treatment of Metastatic Nonsquamous NSCLC (IMpower150)
text: BACKGROUND: IMpower150 evaluated atezolizumab plus bevacizumab plus carboplatin plus paclitaxel (ABCP) versus bevacizumab plus chemotherapy (BCP) in metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC (n=1202). Atezolizumab 1200 mg was given every 3 weeks. RESULTS: Median PFS in the intention-to-treat wild-type population was 8.3 months versus 6.8 months (HR 0.62; 95% CI 0.52-0.74; p<0.001). Median OS was 19.2 months versus 14.7 months (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.64-0.96; p=0.02). Immune-related adverse events included pneumonitis and hepatitis. CONCLUSIONS: ABCP improved PFS and OS versus BCP (NCT02366143).

title: Study of Pembrolizumab versus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in PD-L1 Positive NSCLC (KEYNOTE-024)
text:
Clinical trial NCT02142738.
Title: Study of Pembrolizumab versus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in PD-L1 Positive NSCLC (KEYNOTE-024).
Phase: PHASE3.
Brief summary: Randomized trial of pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w versus platinum chemotherapy in metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS >=50%.
Arms: Experimental: pembrolizumab; Active comparator: platinum chemotherapy.
Interventions: Pembrolizumab (Biological) 200 mg IV every 3 weeks; Chemotherapy (Drug) investigator choice platinum doublet.
Primary endpoints: Progression-free survival.
Serious adverse events: Pneumonitis; Colitis; Hepatitis; Adrenal insufficiency; Infusion related reaction.
